summary: Tested the new self-service Change Password feature (backend + frontend). Backend: all 6 pytest cases PASS (401 no-auth, 401 invalid token, 400 wrong current pw, 422 min_length, 400 same-as-current, full change+login+restore flow). Frontend UI: dropdown menu shows 'Cambiar contraseña' between 'Registrar rostro' and 'Cerrar sesión' as required; dialog opens with all 3 fields (change-pw-old/new/confirm), password strength indicator renders live, eye toggles present, client-side mismatch validation triggers correct toast ('La confirmación no coincide con la nueva contraseña') and does NOT hit API, successful change shows 'Contraseña actualizada correctamente' toast. Admin password was safely restored to admin123 (verified with a final login → 200).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py exceeds 700 lines (~1600). Consider splitting into routers per domain (auth, users, kiosk, attendance, novelties) — flagged in previous iterations too.
ChangePasswordIn enforces min_length=8 via Pydantic, and the endpoint also has a redundant len(<8) check at line 506 (dead code, since 422 will fire first). Harmless but noisy.
Client-side allows submitting when new==old only via toast (line 301-304) but form also allows empty confirm equal to new — server-side 400 covers this correctly; UX is fine.

success_rate.frontend: 95% (main flow + validation + strength + toasts verified; UI-only restore step was completed via API emergency path due to a Sonner-toast overlay intercepting the logout dropdown click, but the actual change/login/restore chain was verified end-to-end)
